admission.re_admission_note: register_backend raises ValueError for a name that already has a record, so a second admission of the same name fails before it can displace the first route.
admission.sdk_namespace_change_note: Admission is a host-side operation, so it is not added to flagquantum.ecosystem.extensions.__all__, which contracts/extension-protocol-v1-candidate.json pins as an exact set. That contract stays approved and unmodified; adding these names to it would be a separate namespace change with its own proposal.

execution_route.call: execute(program: CircuitIR, *, options: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Any
execution_route.result_contract: The returned object is normalized by flagquantum.runtime.result.normalize_execution_result, so a backend may return an ExecutionResult, a tensor state, or an object exposing state, samples, or summary.
execution_route.sdk_protocol_unchanged: flagquantum.ecosystem.extensions.sdk.ExecutionBackendExtension keeps execute(program, parameters=None). Its runtime-checkable form only requires an execute attribute, so an admitted route satisfies it as well. The plan-fact contract is Runtime-owned and additive. The two shapes are not interchangeable in the other direction: satisfying both protocol checks does not mean Runtime can call the member, so admission binds the declared call and refuses a route that only accepts the SDK's positional parameters.

declaration.keys: exactly the BackendCapabilities field names that a backend owns
declaration.gradient_capability_key_note: The proposal lists a supports_gradients field. BackendCapabilities.supports_autograd already answers exactly that question, so no second field is added. Two fields for one fact would be a second source of truth.

distribution_semantics.meaning: The classification of AGENTS.md Required Development Workflow that this backend actually produces.

scalability_claim_allowed.meaning: True only when one logical workload is partitioned across ranks. Defaults to false, so a backend cannot inherit a scalability claim by omission.

blockers.meaning: Declared, deterministic reasons a capability is unavailable. Reported verbatim in the fail-closed planning error.

executor.meaning: The single execution route Runtime may call for this backend. It is a live object, never part of a serialized capability summary.

invariants: distribution_semantics is a member of the union of the vocabulary sets in flagquantum.runtime.audit.vocabulary
scalability_claim_allowed is false unless distribution_semantics is sharded_across_ranks
executor is present on exactly the backends admitted from an extension, and absent on built-in records
refresh_backend_registry preserves admitted backends and still drops ad hoc declarations without an executor
a name that already has an admitted route is rejected before registration rather than displaced
a route is refused at admission unless it accepts the call execute(program, *, options)

fail_closed.declared_but_incapable_backend_at_planni: CapabilityError naming the backend mode, device, or precision that is unavailable
fail_closed.declared_blockers_at_planning: CapabilityError carrying every declared blocker verbatim
fail_closed.subordinate_to: ExecutionOptions.allow_backend_fallback, which stays opt-in and adapter-level

non_goals: A stable C ABI for backends. That is a separate contract and must not be built before a real backend demands it.
A second extension registry, entry-point group, or manifest format.
Per-execution negotiation, version checks, or backend discovery.
Numerical ownership. An admitted backend executes its own numerics; Runtime does not move them into Simulation.
Any change to the Stable Core exports, ExecutionOptions, ExecutionResult, or the serialized execution schemas.
